first_impression.reaction: The intro told us straight away it isn't another random listicle: 'We have followed them in the order families live them, and we have been plain about which details come from UNESCO, the Smithsonian or parish sources and which are simply often told.' That's the kind of honesty we want. And the promise of travel and legal steps for Australians is the bit that actually earned the scroll.

journey.quote: For Australian couples weighing a wedding in Armenia itself, we close with the travel advice and legal steps the listicles skip.
journey.reaction: Good, that's the practical bit we'd actually need. Kept us reading.

journey.quote: treat what follows as a map to talk through with your parents and grandparents, not a rulebook.
journey.reaction: This is the line I'd send to Mum. It doesn't lecture our family about our own traditions.

journey.section: The formal asking and the engagement
journey.quote: We found no official or academic source for them in our research, so what follows is how families often tell it.
journey.reaction: Honest. Though 'often told' gets repeated a lot through the next few sections and starts to read a bit hedgy. Fine, but noticeable.

journey.quote: It asks couples to make contact at least eight months ahead and to confirm the priest and church before booking anything else.
journey.reaction: This is real, usable logistics. We're 14 months out, so this tells us what to do first. Exactly the insider-ish detail we look for.

journey.section: Lavash, honey and the broken plate at the door
journey.quote: For a wedding away from the family home, decide in advance where the "door" will be (a villa entrance, a ballroom foyer) and who will stand in the mother-in-law's place if she cannot travel. Ask the venue where broken crockery can be swept up quickly.
journey.reaction: Best paragraph in the piece for us. Someone has actually thought about how this works at a destination venue. This is what makes us believe a planner could pull it off.

journey.quote: If you want the traditional sound for an entrance or a first dance, book a pair of players rather than a soloist.
journey.reaction: Small, specific, useful. More of this please.

journey.quote: The body is ideally carved from apricot wood, and the longest, at 40 cm, is considered best suited to love songs.
journey.reaction: Nice trivia but this is where I started skimming. The UNESCO detail is a bit encyclopaedic for a planning read.

journey.quote: Level 4, "Do not travel", within 5 km of Armenia's border with Azerbaijan, because of mines and unexploded ordnance.
journey.reaction: Sobering but I'm glad it's said plainly. With half our guests flying in and grandparents to look after, this is exactly what my parents would ask about.

journey.quote: Australia has no embassy or consulate in Armenia, and consular help comes from the Australian Embassy in Moscow.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that. It's the 'something goes wrong and no one is accountable' fear in one sentence. It makes us want to know who on the ground would actually be responsible, and the page doesn't say.

journey.section: Civil registration and the church wedding
journey.quote: We could not read an official Armenian source on this. Check with Armenia's civil registry and the Armenian embassy, including any fees, before you set a date.
journey.reaction: Honest, I respect it as a lawyer. But it means the legal side, which is one of our top three worries, is left entirely to us.

journey.section: Documents, translation and recognition at home (CTA)
journey.quote: You will have a single point of contact, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins; the legal and church paperwork stays with you, the registry and your priest.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing upfront eases the hidden-cost fear. Single point of contact is what we want. But 'the paperwork stays with you' is honest and slightly deflating: so what exactly does 'coordinate' cover? Every planner says end-to-end.

journey.section: Planning the day around your family's traditions
journey.quote: Every Armenian family carries its own version of these customs, and the best weddings make room for the ones that matter most to yours.
journey.reaction: Warm, not cheesy, not salesy. No 'dream day' rubbish anywhere in the piece, which we noticed.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland actually planned an Armenian or Armenian-Australian wedding? Is there a real wedding we can look at, with venue and date?
Do you have your own people on the ground in Armenia, or would you be outsourcing to local suppliers we've never heard of?
Who is accountable on the day if something goes wrong in Yerevan, given there's no Australian embassy there?
What does 'coordinate the venue, travel and suppliers' include in practice: guest airport transfers, accommodation blocks, finding duduk players and a kavor-friendly running sheet?
If we keep the crowning in a Sydney parish and do a destination celebration elsewhere, can you help with that split?
would_share_with: Parents and grandparents (especially the 'map to talk through with your parents and grandparents' and lavash sections)

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like one person to coordinate the venue, travel and suppliers around those answers, [speak with a Wedded Advisor]
cta_reaction.why: Soft and well placed after the legal section, and 'fee agreed in writing' helps. But we'd want to see a real wedding and some proof of experience with Armenian customs or Armenia itself before giving our details. Likely we'd read another post or two first, which is how we work anyway.

top_3_changes: Add one line or link showing Wedded Wonderland's own experience with Armenian or culturally led weddings (a real wedding with venue and date) near the CTA, so we know you've done this before.
Say briefly who is on the ground and accountable on the day for a wedding in Armenia, right after the 'consular help comes from Moscow' line, since that's where the worry peaks.
Trim the encyclopaedic duduk detail and vary the repeated 'often told' phrasing so the middle reads less like a reference entry and keeps the practical tone of the venue tips.
